title: Rishikesh vs Dharamsala: Which Should You Visit?
verdict: Rishikesh for yoga, adventure, and Ganges spirituality. Dharamsala for Tibetan culture, Triund trekking, and mountain peace.

categories.name: Yoga & Meditation
categories.summary: Rishikesh wins yoga — 300+ schools, every style. Dharamsala wins for Tibetan Buddhist meditation and Vipassana.

categories.name: Adventure Sports
categories.summary: Rishikesh dominates — India's best rafting, highest bungee (83m), zip-line, kayaking on the Ganges.

categories.name: Trekking
categories.summary: Dharamsala wins — Triund Trek gives jaw-dropping Dhauladhar views accessible to any fit traveler.

categories.name: Food Scene
categories.summary: Rishikesh wins vegetarian; Dharamsala wins Tibetan momos and meat options. Both excellent, entirely different.

categories.name: Cultural Depth
categories.summary: Dharamsala's Tibetan exile culture is unlike anywhere else in India. Rishikesh offers ancient Hindu pilgrimage culture.

categories.name: Accessibility from Delhi
categories.summary: Rishikesh is 5–6 hours from Delhi. Dharamsala is 12–14 hours by bus or flight via Chandigarh.

categories.name: Budget
categories.summary: Both run ₹1,000–1,800/day without big activities. Rishikesh costs more when doing rafting/bungee.

faq.question: Is Rishikesh or Dharamsala better for yoga?
faq.answer: Rishikesh wins — it's the global yoga capital with 300+ schools and every style of teacher training.

faq.question: What is the Triund Trek?
faq.answer: A 9km day trek from McLeod Ganj to a 2,850m ridge with spectacular Dhauladhar mountain views. No technical skill needed.

faq.question: How far apart are Rishikesh and Dharamsala?
faq.answer: About 500–550km, taking 14–17 hours by bus. They're not a natural combination for a short trip.
